title: Coefficient of x in the expansion of (1+n x) to the power -1
source: Theory P23-7.3 Quick check 1; coefficient of x in (1+n x)^{-1} is -n
stem: Find the coefficient of \(x\) in the expansion of \((1+{n|int}x)^{-1}\) in ascending powers of \(x\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: The x term is n times the first binomial coefficient.

contexts.note: Includes the original (1+3x) to the power -1, coefficient -3

title: Coefficient of x squared in the expansion of (1+n x) to the power -1
source: Theory P23-7.3 Quick check 2; coefficient of x^2 in (1+n x)^{-1} is n squared
stem: Find the coefficient of \(x^2\) in the expansion of \((1+{n|int}x)^{-1}\) in ascending powers of \(x\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: The x squared term uses the second binomial coefficient times n squared.

contexts.note: Includes the original (1+3x) to the power -1, coefficient 9

title: Coefficient of x in the expansion of the square root of 1 minus n x
source: Theory P23-7.3 Quick check 3; coefficient of x in sqrt(1-n x) is -n/2
stem: Find the coefficient of \(x\) in the expansion of \(\sqrt{{1-{n|int}x}}\) in ascending powers of \(x\).

steps.name: A
steps.note: The x term is n times 1/2, with a minus sign.

title: Binomial expansion of the cube root of 1 minus 6x

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem: Expand \(\sqrt[3]{1-6x}\) in ascending powers of \(x\) up to and including the term in \(x^3\), simplifying the coefficients. [4]

steps.name: s1
steps.text_tex: A first-order term of the form \(1+kx\), with \(k=\pm 6\) or \(k=\pm\dfrac{1}{3}\), is obtained.
steps.note: Official MS: M1, obtain 1 + kx, where k = ±6 or ±1/3.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: A1. The official alternative method differentiates to obtain f dash of x = -2(1-6x) to the power -2/3 and hence the same first two terms.

steps.name: s4
steps.text_tex: The term in \(x^3\) is \(-\dfrac{40}{3}x^3\), or an equivalent.
steps.note: Official MS: A1, −40/3 x³ or equivalent.

title: Binomial expansion of 1 over the square root of 1 minus 2x

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem: Expand \(\dfrac{{1}}{{\sqrt{{1-2x}}}}\) in ascending powers of \(x\), up to and including the term in \(x^3\), simplifying the coefficients. [4]

steps.name: s1
steps.text_tex: A correct unsimplified version of the \(x\) or \(x^2\) or \(x^3\) term is stated.
steps.note: Official MS: M1, state a correct un-simplified version of the x or x^2 or x^3 term. Symbolic binomial coefficients are not sufficient for the M mark.

steps.name: s2
steps.note: Official MS: A1, state correct first two terms 1 + x.

steps.name: s3
steps.note: Official MS: A1, obtain the next two terms (3/2)x^2 + (5/2)x^3, first of these two A marks.

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: A1, (5/2)x^3. The expansion is 1 + x + (3/2)x^2 + (5/2)x^3.

title: Binomial expansion of 1 over the cube root of 1 plus 6x

source.note: Stem verbatim from the official QP; marks from the official MS. Question number checked against the QP.

stem: Expand \(\dfrac{{1}}{{\sqrt[{{3}}]{{1+6x}}}}\) in ascending powers of \(x\), up to and including the term in \(x^3\), simplifying the coefficients. [4]

steps.name: s1
steps.text_tex: A correct unsimplified version of the \(x\) or \(x^2\) or \(x^3\) term in the expansion of \((1+6x)^{-1/3}\) is stated.
steps.note: Official MS: M1 (EITHER), state a correct unsimplified version of the x or x-squared or x-cubed term in the expansion of (1+6x) to the power -1/3. Or, differentiate and evaluate f(0) and f-dash(0).

steps.name: s4
steps.note: Official MS: A1, -112/3 x^3 in the final answer.
